evidence.claim: The Kremlin describes Putin as head of state responsible for domestic and foreign-policy direction and Supreme Commander-in-Chief.
evidence.title: Presidential structure

evidence.claim: Putin signed laws criminalizing fake news about the armed forces, calls to end deployment, and support for sanctions, with penalties up to 15 years.
evidence.title: Russia criminalizes independent war reporting and anti-war protests
evidence.excerpt: HRW description of signed censorship and protest laws.
evidence.source_locator: HTML paragraphs describing signed laws and penalties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights documentation of a formal legal act.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct signature by Putin; implementation attribution remains broader.

evidence.claim: OHCHR communication recorded allegations of excessive force, mass arrests, and heightened restrictions during nationwide anti-war protests.
evidence.title: Communication on anti-war protest restrictions
evidence.excerpt: Communication summary of alleged protest abuses.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Allegations concerning Russian authorities; not adjudicated findings.

evidence.claim: Freedom House recorded Memorial’s closure, executive influence over courts, and due-process violations in Russia in 2022.
evidence.title: Russia: Freedom in the World 2022
evidence.excerpt: Country report findings on courts and civil society.
evidence.source_locator: HTML country-report sections on courts and civil society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Country assessment with cited institutional findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National institutional environment; personal attribution limited.

evidence.claim: World Bank reported that Russia’s aggregate GDP contracted 2.1% in 2022 despite sanctions.
evidence.title: Russia economic report
evidence.ruler_attribution: Aggregate outcome; causation and ruler credit unresolved.

evidence.claim: WHO identified strengths and areas for improvement in Russian school-health services.
evidence.title: School health services in the Russian Federation
evidence.ruler_attribution: Service-system context; Putin-specific implementation not established.

evidence.claim: OVD-Info documented police violence during 2022 protests, prosecutions of opposition figures, extremist designations, religious prosecutions, anti-war criminal cases, and civil-society liquidations.
evidence.title: Repressions in Russia in 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Civil-society monitoring report with event detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian authorities and law enforcement; not every incident personally ordered by Putin.

evidence.claim: Amnesty recorded the 24 February Roskomnadzor order requiring media to use official sources and avoid war-related terms, blocking independent media, and the departure of at least 150 journalists.
evidence.title: Russia’s ruthless crackdown stifles independent journalism
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty account of censorship orders and media blocking.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Roskomnadzor and national policy; personal drafting by Putin not established.

evidence.claim: The U.S. State Department’s 2022 report listed credible reports of torture, prison abuses, arbitrary detention, minority violence, media and internet restrictions, political exclusion, and lack of accountability for gender-based violence.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official human-rights reporting; summary is broad.

evidence.claim: Golos reported 4,728 regional and local elections on 11 September 2022, restrictions on candidates, unequal campaigns, limited political rights, and 1,746 reported violations.
evidence.title: Regional and local elections in Russia
evidence.ruler_attribution: Regional electoral environment; Putin’s personal manipulation of each contest not established.

evidence_environment.criticism_possible: Criticism was possible through international organizations, human-rights monitors, election monitors, technical agencies, and public diplomatic records, but domestic criticism was materially constrained. Supported by E001-E003, E007-E011, E015-E016, E021-E029, E035-E038, E047, E049-E052.
evidence_environment.censorship_and_self_censorship: Freedom House, HRW, Amnesty, OVD-Info, and OHCHR material documents censorship, media blocking, foreign-agent or extremist pressure, restricted assembly, and intimidation; these conditions create substantial self-censorship and suppress adverse domestic reporting. Supported by E008-E011, E025-E029, E040-E041.
evidence_environment.safe_reporting_channels: International organizations, foreign-based media, human-rights monitors, election monitors, technical agencies, and public international diplomatic records provided safer reporting channels than domestic independent media. Domestic media and civil-society channels were constrained by the laws and blocking documented in E008, E026-E027, E040-E041.
evidence_environment.official_statistics_reliability: Official statistics and formal records are usable for recorded outputs and macroeconomic conditions but require revision, definition, self-report, and distributional caveats. Rosstat’s revised and unrevised poverty figures differ; Russian Government and Social Fund claims lack independent implementation verification. Supported by E033, E043-E046, E053-E055.
languages_and_archives_searched: English-language UN, OHCHR, IAEA, ICRC, HRW, Freedom House, Amnesty, OVD-Info, IMF, World Bank, WHO, CSIS, ACA, Treasury, OCCRP, DoD, UNODA, State Department, Golos, Rosstat, Bank of Russia, Russian Government, and Social Fund materials.
Russian official government, budget, statistical, central-bank, legal, and Social Fund pages were included where supplied by the researcher.
evidence_environment.source_concentration: Evidence is concentrated among UN/OHCHR, HRW, Freedom House, Amnesty, ICRC, IMF, World Bank, IAEA, and official Russian institutions. Source-family diversity improved through ACA, CSIS, OVD-Info, Golos, OCCRP, Treasury, DoD, UNODA, Rosstat, and Bank of Russia, but several chapters remain monitor- and repression-heavy.
evidence_environment.duplicate_event_risk: Same-source claim families were identified: E006/E018, E019/E020, E021/E039, E026/E040, E027/E041, E034/E046, and E043-E045. These are retained with canonical-key warnings or context disposition and must not be counted as independent corroboration.
evidence_environment.complaint_volume_interpretation: International attention and open reporting overrepresent visible Ukraine-war, opposition, and media cases, while censorship and intimidation suppress less visible complaints. Aggregate welfare indicators may understate unequal hardship rather than complaint severity. Supported by E003, E008-E011, E021-E023, E025-E029, E038-E039, E053-E055.
evidence_environment.relevant_denominators: Relevant denominators include Russia’s population and affected civilian, prisoner, protester, household, regional, and beneficiary populations. The supplied local prior records population LF045; several narrative sources report counts without complete national or exposed-population denominators. This limits generalization.
evidence_environment.inherited_conditions_shocks_and_authorit: Putin’s formal authority is documented by E063. The 2022 invasion, mobilization, attempted annexation, occupation, sanctions, resource dependence, inherited institutional conditions, and pre-existing conflict are confounders across chapters. Local priors are explicitly context rather than direct ruler conduct.
chapter_specific_biases: 1B is affected mainly by secrecy, opaque command structures, and limited technical access.
2B is concentrated on the Ukraine war; battlefield visibility and restricted access jointly distort coverage.
3B is affected by suppressed complaints, prison-access limits, and weak remedy visibility.
4B is concentrated on repression and censorship, with incomplete electoral, judicial, and regional evidence.
5B and 6B rely heavily on aggregate or official statistics that can hide distributional and implementation differences.
7B has a very high personal-attribution risk; network and sanctions evidence must not be converted into proven ownership or criminal liability.
8B is confounded by war, sanctions, inherited capacity, and incomplete program-level implementation evidence.

unresolved_gaps: Primary 2022 Russian nuclear doctrine and internal command-safeguard record.
Complete negotiation decision records, causal attribution, proxy and intelligence evidence.
Domestic prison monitoring, effective remedies, corrective action, minority outcomes, and non-state violence evidence.
Household distribution, realized inflation, housing, sanitation, regional welfare, and independently verified service delivery.
Independently verified Putin-specific beneficial ownership, appointments, conflicts, direct deception, personal benefit, audits, or corrections.
Complete governing-program portfolio with audited implementation, adaptation, durability, and independent outcome evaluation.
Explicit local-data audit mapping remains for parent replacement.
The ten 1B lenses have no matching local structured evidence; this is an explicit local-prior gap, not a zero or score.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Evidence combines local structured priors, UN/OHCHR/IAEA/ICRC, human-rights monitors, technical NGOs, election monitoring, macroeconomic institutions, official Russian records, investigative reporting, and sanctions findings. Source concentration and attribution limitations are explicitly recorded.
